about: How an identity's keys come from its recovery phrase: BIP39 seed (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 rounds, salt "mnemonic"), then SLIP-0010 Ed25519 with every step hardened. Key n of an identity is at m/44'/0'/0'/0'/n': 0 founds it, 1 is what founding commits to, n+1 is what the rotation to key n commits to. public_key_qb64 is the key in CESR with code D. post_quantum: the post-quantum next key of generation j is at m/44'/0'/0'/7000001'/j', ML-DSA-65 from that child seed, qb64 under 2AAE, and its commitment is Blake3-256 over that qb64 text, as code E. messaging: the messaging keyset of generation g is at m/44'/0'/0'/7000002'/g', by its anchor. relationship_post_quantum: the post-quantum next key beside classical key j of a relationship (the owner's own device in an ownership change) is at m/44'/0'/0'/<relationship index>'/(7000001+j)', shown for relationship 1, built as post_quantum is. signature_forms: key 0's signature over the founding, in the A, 2A and B forms. Checked by identity-agent-core/backup and by the app's key manager.
